supersedes: v4 anchor (2026-07-14, 4906.9 rps / p99 37587): retired because it was recorded before two conditions that materially affect the measurement were fixed. (1) The local toolchain was NOT the pinned one: Homebrew's `rust` formula shadowed rustup on PATH, so local cargo builds silently used a different compiler than CI and Bazel. (2) The tree carried a FORKED RustCrypto stack (sha2 0.10 and 0.11 simultaneously), which also broke the Bazel build outright. Both are fixed; this v5 anchor is the first recorded with local == CI == Bazel on one compiler and one crypto generation. v3 anchor (2026-07-14): re-established on the DELEGATED-REQUIRED-ONLY serving path (21f722c, 2026-07-13 — direct-root response signing deleted; the proxy now ALWAYS issues a delegated-credential-backed response signature per request). The prior v2 anchor (5866.4 rps, recorded 2026-07-12) measured the pre-cutover sign_response_full path and is retired: always-delegated-signing costs ~16% throughput (5866.4 -> 4906.9) and ~18% p50 added latency (21450 -> 25334us) on this box, the expected cost of the mandated architecture, not a regression. (The v2 note itself retired the v1 object/JCS carrier baseline.) Same box, same 128/8000/1-core config; the serving path is what changed.
caveat: Recorded on a single developer workstation with the load generator CO-LOCATED with the proxy on the same cores. At the concurrency this anchor uses the run is client-concurrency-bound (128 concurrent cold mTLS handshakes; client-side Ed25519/TLS crypto costs as much as server-side), so throughput is a stable REGRESSION anchor but is NOT a production capacity number, and the 1->N core sweep below is recorded-but-NON-AUTHORITATIVE: on one box the loadgen contends with the fleet for cores and flattens the curve. Authoritative absolute SLOs and the real scaling curve require a dedicated load-generator host driving the proxy on the production hardware class (MCPRE-110 production half; the GKE fleet run, now at the canonical 128/8000 envelope).

recorded.rust_toolchain: 1.97.1 (pinned in rust-toolchain.toml and MODULE.bazel; enforced locally by scripts/use_pinned_toolchain.sh)
recorded.serving_mode: delegated-required-only (ADR-MCPRE-052; delegated-credential-backed response signature per request)
recorded.carrier: RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures + RFC 9530 Content-Digest (signature in HTTP headers; no object/JCS _meta signature)
recorded.crypto_generation: RustCrypto digest 0.11 (sha2 0.11, ed25519-dalek 3, hmac 0.13, curve25519-dalek 5) — ONE generation; //deny.toml denies a second via deny-multiple-versions

anchor.comment: The regression anchor on the delegated-required serving path: single served core, moderate concurrency (least loadgen-distorted, most reproducible). Values are the MEDIAN of 6 reps on a developer workstation with co-located loadgen. Recorded on a QUIET box (background kind clusters stopped, load average ~3.6) and with the toolchain pinned via rust-toolchain.toml + scripts/use_pinned_toolchain.sh, so the compiler that produced these numbers is the one CI uses. Throughput spread is 5486.0-5555.7 (+/-0.6%, far tighter than the v4 anchor's +/-3%); the p99 spread (37877-49339) is wider because the co-located load GENERATOR is descheduled by desktop background activity and that jitter is measured client-side. adr051_slo_gate.py compares a fresh run of THIS config against these numbers.

recorded_core_sweep_non_authoritative.comment: PRE-CUTOVER, retained for the record only (measured on the old sign_response_full path, 2026-07-12) and NON-AUTHORITATIVE: throughput is flat-to-noisy as served cores rise because the co-located loadgen is the limiter, not per-core scaling. Do NOT gate on this curve; the authoritative 1->N curve is the GKE fleet run.
